Querying a store with DuckDB

Source: vignettes/duckdb.Rmd
duckdb.Rmd

DuckDB is a database that runs inside the R process and reads Parquet files directly. rcs opens a whole store in DuckDB with one call: every dataset becomes a view, a named query over the dataset’s files. No data is copied; DuckDB reads the files when a query runs, and only the columns and row groups the query needs. SQL and dbplyr then work on the store, joins between datasets included, and results can be written back to the store without passing through R as a whole.

This vignette needs the packages duckdb, DBI and dbplyr. It works with a store in a local folder; the last sections say what changes on Google Cloud Storage. vignette("rcs") introduces stores and store_open().

library(rcs)

A store to work with

A store with two datasets: a table of simulated daily sales, one file per year, and simulated polygons, a geospatial dataset with its H3 index table.

path <- file.path(tempdir(), "duckdb-store")
st <- store_connect(path, create = TRUE)

store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(500, seed = 1), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales",
  description = "Simulated daily sales by shop and product.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"),
  partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 500 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary  <tempdir>/duckdb-store  2/2 files sent  38.2 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
store_write(st, rcs_sim_polygons(300, seed = 3), "shapes/polygons",
  title = "Polygons",
  description = "Simulated polygons in open ocean.",
  key = "id"
)
#> ℹ Writing "shapes/polygons": 300 rows in 1 file, and its index table in 1 file.
#> ✔ primary  <tempdir>/duckdb-store  2/2 files sent  51.9 kB  0.3s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.

Views in memory

store_duckdb() creates a DuckDB connection, here an in-memory database, with one view per dataset of the store (rasters excluded, index tables included), and returns the connection invisibly.

con <- store_duckdb(st)
#> ✔ DuckDB views (native mode, nothing read yet): `sales.daily`,
#> `shapes.polygons`, and `shapes.polygons__h3`.

The first part of a dataset’s name is the schema, the other parts, joined with __, are the view: sales/daily is the view sales.daily, and the index table of shapes/polygons is shapes.polygons__h3. A dataset with a one-part name goes to the schema main. Two datasets that would get the same view name abort, as does a first part rcs or one equal to the name of an attached database (such as memory).

Views are queried with SQL like tables:

DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT year, count(*) AS n, sum(qty) AS qty
  FROM sales.daily
  GROUP BY year
  ORDER BY year
")
#>   year   n  qty
#> 1 2023 252 5851
#> 2 2024 248 6065

and can be joined. Here each polygon is joined with its rows in the index table, the H3 cells it touches; the macro rcs_h3_hex(), defined on every connection the package prepares, shows a cell, stored as a 64-bit integer, as its hex code:

DBI::dbGetQuery(con, '
  SELECT p.id, count(*) AS cells, rcs_h3_hex(min(i.h3)) AS first_cell
  FROM shapes.polygons AS p
  JOIN shapes.polygons__h3 AS i USING (".rcs_id")
  GROUP BY p.id
  ORDER BY cells DESC, p.id
  LIMIT 3
')
#>   id cells      first_cell
#> 1  1   212 85565907fffffff
#> 2  3    41 857c584bfffffff
#> 3  2    29 85564823fffffff

H3 cells are BIGINT columns. The connections the package makes use bigint = "integer64", so that cells reach R as bit64::integer64 values: a double cannot hold a cell exactly. A connection you make yourself and pass to the package must use the same setting, or the call aborts.

What a connection holds

store_tables() lists the views of a connection, with the dataset and the version each one shows. Given the store as well, the column current says whether a view shows the version in the store’s catalog.

store_tables(con, st)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   schema name         type  dataset             version          current
#> * <chr>  <chr>        <chr> <chr>               <chr>            <lgl>  
#> 1 sales  daily        view  sales/daily         b454e301a840470a TRUE   
#> 2 shapes polygons     view  shapes/polygons     7d045aaa53d8b240 TRUE   
#> 3 shapes polygons__h3 view  shapes/polygons__h3 e72b28d7c379c808 TRUE

Given a store, it lists the datasets with the name of the view each one gets:

store_tables(st)[c("dataset", "kind", "rows", "duckdb_view")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   dataset         kind        rows duckdb_view    
#>   <chr>           <chr>      <dbl> <chr>          
#> 1 sales/daily     table        500 sales.daily    
#> 2 shapes/polygons geospatial   300 shapes.polygons

The connection records its views in the table rcs.views and the store’s locations in rcs.store. Neither holds a credential. A connection serves one store: preparing it for a second store aborts.

DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT view, dataset, mode FROM rcs.views")
#>                  view             dataset   mode
#> 1         sales.daily         sales/daily native
#> 2     shapes.polygons     shapes/polygons native
#> 3 shapes.polygons__h3 shapes/polygons__h3 native

store_duckdb(st, datasets = ) adds or refreshes the views of some datasets only (with their index tables) and leaves the others alone; without datasets, every view is refreshed and the views of datasets no longer in the catalog are dropped.

Two modes

store_duckdb() has two modes, which differ in who reads the files.

  • mode = "native" (the default): each view is a read_parquet() query over the dataset’s file list, and DuckDB reads the files itself. The views are plain query text, so they keep working in a database file after it is reopened (see below). The geometry column of a geospatial dataset has the DuckDB type GEOMETRY. On a bucket, DuckDB needs a credential of its own, which the package gives it (see “Buckets”).
  • mode = "arrow": the Arrow dataset that the package opens for its own reads is registered in DuckDB, and the view selects from it. DuckDB needs no credential, filters are passed into the Arrow scan, and geometry is WKB (a BLOB). The registration lives only as long as the connection.
con_arrow <- store_duckdb(st, mode = "arrow")
#> ✔ DuckDB views (arrow mode, nothing read yet): `sales.daily`,
#> `shapes.polygons`, and `shapes.polygons__h3`.
DBI::dbGetQuery(con_arrow, "SELECT count(*) AS n FROM sales.daily WHERE year = 2024")
#>     n
#> 1 248
DBI::dbDisconnect(con_arrow, shutdown = TRUE)

In both modes each dataset is read from the location a read with store_read() would use, and the views show the versions of the catalog held by st. After store_refresh(st) or a write through another connection, call store_duckdb() again.

spatial = TRUE also installs and loads DuckDB’s spatial extension (downloaded on first use), and in arrow mode adds a column geom of type GEOMETRY to geospatial views, for DuckDB’s spatial functions.

con_spatial <- store_duckdb(st, mode = "arrow", spatial = TRUE)
DBI::dbGetQuery(con_spatial, "SELECT id, ST_Area(geom) AS area FROM shapes.polygons LIMIT 3")
DBI::dbDisconnect(con_spatial, shutdown = TRUE)

dbplyr tables

store_open(engine = "duckdb") returns a dbplyr table on a dataset’s view. With con, the view is made (or refreshed) on that connection; without it, on an in-memory connection the package keeps for the store until the end of the session. Every dbplyr verb works, and the table prints as any dbplyr table.

daily <- store_open(st, "daily", engine = "duckdb", con = con)
daily |>
  dplyr::filter(year == 2024) |>
  dplyr::count(product, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(3) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   product       n
#>   <fct>   <int64>
#> 1 p17          24
#> 2 p04          18
#> 3 p02          17

Inside DuckDB, values keep the types they are stored with: a factor is text, a time difference a number. collect() on a table made by store_open() restores the R types from the catalog, as the Arrow engine does: factor levels, difftime units, 64-bit integers, and H3 cells as rcs_h3 vectors printed as hex. A geospatial dataset comes back as an sf object with the catalog’s coordinate reference system, without the row identifier .rcs_id.

daily |>
  dplyr::filter(year == 2024, qty > 48) |>
  dplyr::select(shop_id, date, product, grade, wait) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   shop_id date       product grade wait       
#>     <int> <date>     <fct>   <ord> <drtn>     
#> 1       4 2024-11-26 p15     mid    9.44 hours
#> 2      10 2024-02-24 p07     low    0.70 hours
#> 3      12 2024-06-12 p17     mid   51.88 hours
#> 4      14 2024-04-25 p06     mid   37.39 hours
#> 5      19 2024-08-26 p07     mid    0.78 hours
#> 6      20 2024-10-01 p05     high  10.82 hours

A plain dplyr::tbl(con, DBI::Id(schema = "sales", table = "daily")) gives the same rows with DuckDB’s types. store_restore_types() restores the types of any data frame from a dataset’s catalog entry.

Spatial filter in DuckDB

store_intersects() works on a table made by store_open(engine = "duckdb"). The candidate test is added to the table’s SQL: the box test on bbox and, for queries that fill little of their bounding box (a thin diagonal strip, a line), the H3 cells with the index view. The table must still hold those columns, so call it before a select() that drops them.

area <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(
  c(xmin = -28, ymin = 7, xmax = -27, ymax = 8),
  crs = sf::st_crs(4326)
))
polygons <- store_open(st, "polygons", engine = "duckdb", con = con)

exact says where the exact test runs:

  • exact = TRUE (the default): in R, in collect(), on the candidate rows, with the same engine as the Arrow path. The rows are exactly those of store_open(st, "polygons") |> store_intersects(area) |> collect().
  • exact = FALSE: no exact test; the result is the candidate set, which holds every intersecting row and may hold others, with a message saying so.
  • exact = "sql": in DuckDB, with ST_Intersects() of the spatial extension (installed and loaded when needed). The query stays lazy, so the result can be aggregated or joined in DuckDB. The test is in the plane of the coordinates: the rows are those of the Arrow path with exact_engine = "planar", except for queries across the antimeridian or around a pole.
polygons |>
  store_intersects(area) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  nrow()
#> [1] 15

polygons |>
  store_intersects(area, exact = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  nrow()
#> ℹ Spatial filter: `exact = FALSE`, so the result is the candidate set.
#>   It holds every intersecting row and may hold rows that do not intersect the query.
#> [1] 15
polygons |>
  store_intersects(area, exact = "sql") |>
  dplyr::count(cat)

Several calls combine: a row must intersect every query. A count or other aggregate computed in DuckDB after a pending exact test (exact = TRUE) counts the candidate rows, since the exact test runs only in collect(); use exact = "sql" for that. A query of more than 10,000 H3 cells puts the cells in a temporary table on the connection, kept until it is closed.

Writing from DuckDB

store_write() accepts a lazy table on a DuckDB connection: a dbplyr query on the views, on your own tables, or both. The result is stored without being collected into R as a whole.

by_product <- dplyr::tbl(con, DBI::Id(schema = "sales", table = "daily")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(year, product) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    qty = as.integer(sum(qty, na.rm = TRUE)),
    days = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

store_write(st, by_product, "sales/by_product",
  title = "Sales by product and year",
  description = "Quantity sold and number of rows per product and year.",
  key = c("year", "product")
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/by_product": 38 rows in 1 file.
#> ✔ primary  <tempdir>/duckdb-store  1/1 files sent  3.2 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 1 file in 1 location. Catalogs updated.

How it works:

  • The query runs once inside DuckDB into a temporary copy, a table rcs_write_<random> on the same connection. Every later step reads that copy, and it is dropped when the call ends, also after an error. It needs room in DuckDB’s memory or its temporary folder.
  • The key is checked and the partitions are listed in DuckDB. Then the rows are fetched in batches of getOption("rcs.duckdb_batch_rows") rows (5e5 by default), sorted as the package sorts them, and streamed into the Parquet files; R holds about one batch at a time. A progress bar shows the batches of a long write.
  • The files are staged, checked and land in every location as for any other write; DuckDB never uploads. They are identical to those written from the same rows collected into R, so both give the same version.
  • Modes "create" and "replace" work; "update" aborts.
  • Types: integers, doubles, text, dates and logicals are stored as they are, BIGINT as 64-bit integers (bit64::integer64 in R), TIMESTAMP without time zone and TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE in UTC. HUGEINT, UHUGEINT, INTERVAL, UNION and MAP columns abort, naming the columns. DuckDB’s sum() of an integer column is a HUGEINT; that is why the query above casts it with as.integer().
  • Values keep their DuckDB types: a factor read through a view is text, and is stored as text.

A table with a column geometry, WKB (BLOB) or GEOMETRY, is written as a geospatial dataset, and crs must give its coordinate reference system. The geometries pass through R in batches: per batch, the bounding boxes, the H3 cells and the index rows are computed as for an sf object, with the same geocoding engine and warning (see ?store_write). The rows are then sorted and written from DuckDB. The columns .rcs_id, h3, bbox and geom of the input are the package’s own: they are dropped with a message and computed again.

cat_a <- polygons |>
  dplyr::filter(cat == "a") |>
  dplyr::select(id, area, geometry)

store_write(st, cat_a, "shapes/cat_a",
  title = "Polygons of category a",
  description = "The polygons of category a, written from DuckDB.",
  key = "id", crs = 4326
)
#> ℹ Writing "shapes/cat_a": 59 rows in 1 file, and its index table in 1 file.
#> ✔ primary  <tempdir>/duckdb-store  2/2 files sent  23.0 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.

partition = "h3", geocode = FALSE and geocode_engine work as for an sf object.

A database file

With path, the views live in a DuckDB database file, created when missing, together with any table or view you create in it. The file must lie outside the folders of the store (a sync would carry it along). A file work.duckdb is attached as the database work, so no dataset of the store may have the first part work.

DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

db <- file.path(tempdir(), "analysis.duckdb")
con <- store_duckdb(st, path = db)
#> ✔ DuckDB views (native mode, nothing read yet): `sales.by_product`, `sales.daily`, `shapes.cat_a`, `shapes.cat_a__h3`,
#>   `shapes.polygons`, and `shapes.polygons__h3`.

A view is query text, so the file stays small whatever the size of the datasets. Your own tables sit next to the views. The cell column is named cell here, because a column h3 of a table written with store_write() is taken as the package’s own and dropped.

DBI::dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE TABLE main.cell_counts AS
  SELECT h3 AS cell, count(*) AS polygons
  FROM shapes.polygons__h3
  GROUP BY h3
")
#> [1] 366
store_tables(con, st)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 6
#>   schema name         type  dataset             version          current
#> * <chr>  <chr>        <chr> <chr>               <chr>            <lgl>  
#> 1 main   cell_counts  table NA                  NA               NA     
#> 2 sales  by_product   view  sales/by_product    b5d62d115f8723b8 TRUE   
#> 3 sales  daily        view  sales/daily         b454e301a840470a TRUE   
#> 4 shapes cat_a        view  shapes/cat_a        fa75cbab22985b29 TRUE   
#> 5 shapes cat_a__h3    view  shapes/cat_a__h3    e8056628ad9ec1c5 TRUE   
#> 6 shapes polygons     view  shapes/polygons     7d045aaa53d8b240 TRUE   
#> 7 shapes polygons__h3 view  shapes/polygons__h3 e72b28d7c379c808 TRUE
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

Reopening

Call store_duckdb(st, path = db) again to reopen the file. It refreshes the file to the catalog of st: views of new datasets are added, views of deleted datasets dropped, every view points to the current version, the credentials are renewed, and your own tables and views are left as they are. A table or a view of yours that has the name of a dataset’s view aborts, naming it.

store_duckdb(path = db), without st, reads the store’s locations from the table rcs.store in the file, connects to the store with default credentials, and refreshes the same way:

con <- store_duckdb(path = db)
#> ✔ DuckDB views (native mode, nothing read yet): `sales.by_product`, `sales.daily`, `shapes.cat_a`, `shapes.cat_a__h3`,
#>   `shapes.polygons`, and `shapes.polygons__h3`.
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM main.cell_counts ORDER BY polygons DESC, cell LIMIT 3")
#>                 cell polygons
#> 1 600496714289250303        3
#> 2 600496811999756287        3
#> 3 600497847086874623        3
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

The file is also a plain DuckDB database: DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(dbdir = db), bigint = "integer64") opens it without rcs. Your tables then work, and native views work as long as their files exist, with these limits:

  • the views show the versions of the last refresh. A store without history deletes the files of a replaced version, so a view of a dataset written since then fails until the file is refreshed;
  • views on Google Cloud Storage need a DuckDB secret first;
  • views in arrow mode do not work until store_duckdb() is called again (it says so when it prepares them in a file).

store_tables(con, st) shows which views are no longer current. Here the daily sales are written again with changed quantities, and the file is opened without rcs:

sales <- rcs_sim_table(500, seed = 1)
sales$qty <- sales$qty + 1L
store_write(st, sales, "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales",
  description = "Simulated daily sales by shop and product.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"),
  partition = "year",
  mode = "replace"
)
#> ℹ Replacing "sales/daily": 500 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary  <tempdir>/duckdb-store  2/2 files sent  38.2 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(dbdir = db), bigint = "integer64")
store_tables(con, st)[c("schema", "name", "type", "current")]
#> # A tibble: 7 × 4
#>   schema name         type  current
#>   <chr>  <chr>        <chr> <lgl>  
#> 1 main   cell_counts  table NA     
#> 2 sales  by_product   view  TRUE   
#> 3 sales  daily        view  FALSE  
#> 4 shapes cat_a        view  TRUE   
#> 5 shapes cat_a__h3    view  TRUE   
#> 6 shapes polygons     view  TRUE   
#> 7 shapes polygons__h3 view  TRUE
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

store_duckdb(st, path = db) brings the view up to date.

The local-first workflow

DuckDB and a local store together make a complete workplace on one machine, with no cloud credential:

  1. Keep the store in a local folder and write to it as usual.
  2. Open it in a DuckDB file with store_duckdb(st, path = ); build aggregations, joins and your own tables in SQL or dbplyr.
  3. Write the results that should be kept back to the store with store_write(), from DuckDB directly.
  4. Reopen the file any time with store_duckdb(), which refreshes the views.
con <- store_duckdb(st, path = db)
#> ✔ DuckDB views (native mode, nothing read yet): `sales.by_product`, `sales.daily`, `shapes.cat_a`, `shapes.cat_a__h3`,
#>   `shapes.polygons`, and `shapes.polygons__h3`.
cells <- dplyr::tbl(con, DBI::Id(schema = "main", table = "cell_counts")) |>
  dplyr::filter(polygons > 1)
store_write(st, cells, "shapes/shared_cells",
  title = "Shared cells",
  description = "H3 cells touched by more than one polygon.",
  key = "cell"
)
#> ℹ Writing "shapes/shared_cells": 70 rows in 1 file.
#> ✔ primary  <tempdir>/duckdb-store  1/1 files sent  2.3 kB  0.1s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 1 file in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
  1. When the work is ready to share, add a bucket as a secondary location and copy the store there with store_sync() (see vignette("locations")). Only then are cloud credentials needed.
st <- store_connect(path, secondary = "gs://my-bucket/store", create = TRUE)
store_sync(st)

Afterwards every write reaches both locations, and reads, DuckDB views included, keep using the local copy.

Buckets

On Google Cloud Storage nothing changes in the calls; only who reads the files does. In arrow mode, Arrow reads them with the connection’s credentials (see vignette("locations")), as for any read. In native mode DuckDB reads them itself, through its httpfs extension (downloaded on first use), and needs a credential: store_duckdb() creates for each bucket location a temporary DuckDB secret from the location’s credential. The secret lives only in this connection; it is never written to the database file, to the store or to an environment variable.

st <- store_connect("gs://my-bucket/store")
con <- store_duckdb(st, path = "~/work/analysis.duckdb")
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT year, sum(qty) AS qty FROM sales.daily GROUP BY year")

A secret holds an access token, not a key, and the token is valid for about an hour. After an hour of DuckDB work on a bucket, call store_duckdb() again: every call renews the secrets (and refreshes the views).

con <- store_duckdb(st, path = "~/work/analysis.duckdb")

A credential that DuckDB cannot use (the ambient credential of a Google Cloud machine without a key file) aborts in native mode; use mode = "arrow" there. store_auth_check(st) reports whether DuckDB, and each other client, can read each location.
